issues.t: Hybrid (IMA) battery pack failing
issues.sym: The IMA warning light comes on, electric boost fades or disappears, the battery gauge on the dash jumps up and down, and the car may force-charge constantly. A badly failed pack can even leave the car unable to start.
issues.why: The nickel-metal hydride hybrid pack loses capacity with age and heat, and its cells drift out of balance. Honda issued warranty extensions and product updates for early pack failures on these cars, but those programs have long since ended.
issues.next: Have the hybrid system scanned by a hybrid specialist. Many owners choose a reconditioned or new aftermarket pack rather than a dealer pack, and a healthy 12V battery is needed for an accurate diagnosis.

issues.t: CVT judder or slipping (automatic cars)
issues.sym: On cars with the automatic (CVT), a shudder when pulling away from a stop, a feeling of slipping, the engine revving without matching speed, or loss of drive.
issues.why: The CVT's start clutch can judder and the drive belt can slip as the transmission wears. Honda ran service campaigns with extended coverage for start clutch judder and belt slippage on these cars, and owners report CVT failures around 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the CVT fluid checked and the transmission scanned. Early judder may improve with fresh Honda CVT fluid and a software update, but slipping usually means a rebuilt or used transmission.

issues.t: Catalytic converter wearing out
issues.sym: Check engine light, a failed emissions test, a sulfur smell, or poorer fuel economy.
issues.why: The lean-burn engine on manual cars runs very lean, which works the catalytic converter hard. Owners report the main converter wearing out around 100,000 miles, and Honda issued a bulletin for check engine lights caused by a worn converter.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the oxygen sensors checked first. If the converter is confirmed bad, replace it with one that is legal in your state.

issues.t: EGR passages clogging with carbon
issues.sym: Rough running, hesitation, misfires, or a check engine light, often slowly getting worse.
issues.why: Carbon builds up on the EGR valve and the plate that feeds exhaust gas back into the intake. Owners report needing to clean it every 20,000–30,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the EGR valve and plate inspected and cleaned. Cleaning is cheap compared with replacing parts, and doing it regularly prevents repeat trouble.

issues.t: Air-fuel (wideband oxygen) sensor failure
issues.sym: Check engine light, worse fuel economy, and lean-burn mode no longer working.
issues.why: The lean-burn engine needs a special wideband air-fuel sensor that costs much more than a normal oxygen sensor. Owners report it often fails around 60,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If the air-fuel sensor is at fault, use a Honda or exact-match sensor; cheap universal sensors can cause new problems.

issues.t: IMA light with no assist and stalling at stops
issues.sym: The IMA light comes on with little or no electric assist, auto idle-stop stops working, or the engine stalls after a stop and won't restart in gear.
issues.why: Honda issued several bulletins for IMA codes on these years, covering control software, battery wiring and the battery junction board. Faults in the IMA electronics can shut down assist even when the pack itself is fine.
issues.next: Have the IMA codes read by someone who knows these cars. Check the 12V battery and IMA wiring connections before buying an expensive battery pack.

issues.t: Won't start in very cold weather or with a weak 12V battery
issues.sym: The car cranks slowly or not at all on very cold mornings, or the hybrid system acts oddly, with warning lights and weak assist.
issues.why: These cars normally start the engine using the hybrid motor and only use the small backup starter in extreme cold. Honda issued a bulletin for no-starts below about 0°F, and a weak 12V battery confuses the hybrid system.
issues.next: Test the 12V battery and replace it if weak. In very cold climates, a block heater or garage parking helps.

issues.t: EVAP leak codes P1456 or P1457
issues.sym: Check engine light with an evaporative emissions code, but the car drives normally.
issues.why: Leaks in the fuel vapor system, or a failed EVAP bypass solenoid, set these codes. Honda issued bulletins on diagnosing them.
issues.next: Check that the fuel cap clicks tight first. If the light returns, have a smoke test done to find the leak.

issues.t: Heater blower motor stops or blows fuse
issues.sym: The fan quits working, sometimes after running on high, and the blower fuse is found blown.
issues.why: Honda issued a bulletin for the heater blower motor overheating or blowing its fuse on early Insights.
issues.next: Have the fuse and blower checked. A blower motor that keeps blowing fuses should be replaced.

issues.t: Speedometer and odometer read high
issues.sym: The speedometer shows a little more than your real speed and the odometer adds miles faster than you actually drive.
issues.why: Honda found the speedometer and odometer on many models of this era read slightly high. It issued a bulletin and, after a class-action settlement, extended warranty mileage on affected cars.
issues.next: Check your speed against a GPS app. The settlement coverage has ended, but knowing about it helps when judging the mileage on a used car.

issues.t: Low-beam headlights can suddenly go out (recall)
issues.sym: The low beams flicker or go dark without warning, especially after long use at night.
issues.why: A terminal in the headlight wiring connector can overheat and burn, cutting power to the low beams.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 04V-086 and have the switch and connector inspected. Don't drive at night if the low beams flicker.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you can see or feel; the risk only shows up in a crash.
issues.why: Some passenger airbag modules had poor welds and may not inflate properly.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 02V-196 and have the module replaced if it was never done.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, the low oil light comes on, or you see blue smoke. Some engines eventually misfire or fail.
issues.why: Oil gets past the piston rings and is burned in the engine. This is the most-reported problem on the second-generation Insight, especially the 2012 model.
issues.next: Check the oil every few fill-ups and keep it topped up. Ask a Honda dealer to do an oil consumption test, and keep records in case goodwill help is offered.

issues.t: IMA battery deterioration code P0A7F
issues.sym: The IMA light and check engine light come on, electric assist fades, and fuel economy drops.
issues.why: The hybrid battery loses capacity over time. Honda released battery control software updates for 2010-2012 Insights to deal with a memory effect and the P0A7F code.
issues.next: Ask a Honda dealer whether the battery software update has been done. If the pack is truly worn out, a new or reconditioned pack is the fix.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you notice day to day. In a crash, the inflator could burst and throw metal pieces.
issues.why: The Takata driver airbag inflator can degrade from humidity and heat over the years.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 16V-061 and 19V-500 and get the free replacement right away.

issues.t: Passenger airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you notice day to day. The danger is in a crash.
issues.why: The Takata passenger airbag inflator can break down after years of heat and humidity and burst when it deploys.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 16V-346, 17V-030, 18V-042, 18V-661 and 19V-502 and have the inflator replaced for free.

issues.t: Replacement passenger airbag may be installed wrong (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. The airbag may not open correctly in a crash.
issues.why: Some replacement passenger airbag modules fitted during earlier repairs may not have been installed correctly.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 18V-268 and 19V-378 so the dealer can inspect the installation.

issues.t: Roof molding coming loose
issues.sym: Wind noise or flapping at speed, or a roof trim strip lifting at one end.
issues.why: The clips that hold the roof moldings can loosen. Honda released an update and service bulletin for it.
issues.next: Have the molding re-secured before it tears off on the highway. Ask a dealer about the bulletin.

issues.t: Check engine light for EVAP leak from fuel cap
issues.sym: A check engine light with code P0455 or P0456, with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: Honda issued a bulletin linking these evaporative leak codes to a loose or faulty fuel cap.
issues.next: Tighten the cap until it clicks. If the light comes back, replace the cap, then have the system smoke-tested if needed.

issues.t: Fuel pump may fail (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, sputtering, the check engine light, stalling while driving, or the engine not starting.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump inside the tank can stop working.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 20V-314, 21V-215 and 23V-858. A stall at speed is a crash risk, so get the free pump replacement soon.

issues.t: Fuel pump can stop working on some 2022 cars (recall)
issues.sym: The engine may run poorly, stall while driving, or fail to start.
issues.why: Some 2022 Insights were added to Honda's expanded fuel pump recall because the in-tank pump can fail.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 23V-858 and have the pump module replaced for free.

issues.t: A/C blows warm (condenser leak)
issues.sym: Air from the vents gets warm or only slightly cool, often after a couple of years.
issues.why: Some A/C condensers were not made to specification and can corrode through, letting refrigerant leak. Honda extended condenser coverage to 10 years with unlimited miles.
issues.next: Have the A/C leak-tested at a Honda dealer and ask whether the extended condenser warranty covers it.

issues.t: 12V battery stops charging, car may lose power (recall)
issues.sym: Warning lights, a dead or weak 12V battery, and in the worst case loss of drive power while driving.
issues.why: The DC-DC converter that charges the 12V battery from the hybrid system can shut itself down because of a software fault.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 20V-798 and get the free software update.

issues.t: Wipers, lights or camera may stop working (recall)
issues.sym: Wipers, defroster, rearview camera, exterior lights or power windows act up or stop working.
issues.why: A software error can disrupt communication with the body control module that runs these features.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 20V-771 and have the software updated.

issues.t: Passenger seat sensor can crack and set off the airbag (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light, or a passenger airbag that is not turned off when it should be.
issues.why: The front passenger seat weight sensor can crack and short circuit, which confuses the airbag system.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 24V-064 and 26V-332. If the airbag light is on, get it checked before carrying a front passenger.

issues.t: Rearview camera image may not appear (recall)
issues.sym: The center screen doesn't show the backup camera picture when in reverse.
issues.why: A fault in the center display can stop it from showing the camera view.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 18V-629 and get the update. Look over your shoulder when backing until it is fixed.

issues.t: Airbags and belt tensioners may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light may come on, or there may be no sign at all.
issues.why: A manufacturing error in the airbag (SRS) control unit can keep airbags and seat belt tensioners from firing in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 18V-664 and have the control unit replaced.

issues.t: Front seat belt may not latch (recall)
issues.sym: The front seat belt won't click in, or seems latched but pulls out.
issues.why: A part of the buckle can block the release button so the latch doesn't fully engage.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 23V-158. Always tug the belt after buckling until it is repaired.

issues.t: Rear center belt may not hold a child seat (recall)
issues.sym: The second-row center belt doesn't lock when pulled all the way out to secure a car seat, or unlocks on its own.
issues.why: The automatic locking feature of the rear center belt retractor may switch off too early, leaving a child seat loose.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 21V-900. Use the LATCH anchors or another seat for a child seat until it's fixed.

issues.t: Touchscreen freezing or rebooting
issues.sym: The infotainment screen freezes, goes black, restarts on its own, or drops phone connection.
issues.why: Owners report software crashes in the audio and touchscreen unit.
issues.next: Ask a Honda dealer for any available software update, and try a reset by turning the car fully off for a few minutes.

issues.t: Sudden braking with no obstacle ahead
issues.sym: The car brakes hard or flashes a 'BRAKE' warning on its own when nothing is in the way.
issues.why: Owners report the collision mitigation braking system misreading things like shadows, signs or passing cars.
issues.next: Report it to NHTSA and a Honda dealer. Keep the radar and windshield camera area clean, and ask about software updates.
